HACKATHON GUARDRAILS (non-negotiable):
- DEADLINE: 2026-10-12T18:25Z. Feature freeze 2026-10-12T06:25Z. You work on ONE task; stop when its acceptance passes.
- Read docs/DESIGN.md sections named in your task before writing code. src/types.ts is the shared contract:
  if you need a change, make it minimal and say so in your final message.
- Touch only the files your task OWNS. Never edit another task's files, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, setups/, experiments/.
- Tests: `bun test <your test path>` must pass and `bun test` (whole suite) must not regress. Never modify existing tests
  unless your task says so. Fixtures are built by scripts from real samples, never hand-invented payloads.
- Commit in small steps as work lands, message prefix "<task id>: ". Never rewrite history. Never commit secrets or .env.
- Never describe unbuilt work as done in README/docs. No numbers in docs except those generated into docs/FACTS.md.
- Use `entire graph impact --symbol <name> --json` (or `entire graph query`) before editing an existing module, if available.
- Final message: what you built, test output summary, any types.ts change, anything you could not finish.

TASK T16 · W5 · Task ledger for our own build
GOAL: Record every build task's setup, prompt hash, branch, merge commit and Entire session, so our own repo is a labelled dataset.
READ: docs/DESIGN.md §"Self-build protocol".
OWNS: scripts/ledger.ts, reports/self/tasks.jsonl (append-only, created by the script), tests/ledger.test.ts
BUILD: `bun scripts/ledger.ts record <Txx> <setup> <branch>` (called by run-setup.sh at start) and `... merged <Txx> <mergeSha>`;
`... sync` reads the Entire-Checkpoint trailers on each task branch and fills session ids; `... check` verifies every merged task
has ≥ 1 checkpoint and that its prompt tag matches its recorded setup. Lines: {task, setup, branch, started_at, prompt_sha256,
merge_sha, checkpoint_ids[], user_prompts, human_commits}.
ACCEPTANCE: tests on a temp git repo with fake trailers; `check` flags a tag/setup mismatch.
TEST: bun test tests/ledger.test.ts
DO NOT TOUCH: anything outside OWNS (run-setup.sh is ops; propose its one-line hook in your final message).

52:### Self-build protocol
53-This is what makes this repo a labelled dataset.
54-1. **Task ids and assignment.** Every build task has an id `Txx` and a seeded random setup assignment (seed `20261010`). Both are published in `experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md`.
55-2. **Prompt tag.** The first prompt of every session starts with `[roster setup=<id> task=<Txx>]`. Roster's own setup inference is checked against these tags.
56-3. **One task per worktree.** One task gets one worktree and one branch, launched by `scripts/run-setup.sh <setup> <task>` with isolated settings: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config`. The project `.mcp.json` holds only Entire and neatlogs.
57-4. **Merging.** Merge with `git merge --no-ff`. **Never squash**: squashing drops the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers that attribution depends on.
58-5. **Commit prefixes.** Human fixes are separate commits prefixed `human:`. Operational work is prefixed `ops:` and excluded from every experiment.
59-
60-## Entire checkpoint format
61-
62-This section was verified on 2026-10-10 against 6 public repos (2,421 session rows). Redacted real samples are in `tests/fixtures/samples/`. Build against them.
63-
64-### Two storage backends (read both)
65-
66-| Backend | Where | Layout | Checkpoint id |
67-|---|---|---|---|
68-| `branch` (legacy, visible on GitHub) | `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1`, one cumulative tree | `<id[0:2]>/<id[2:]>/…` | 12 hex chars, e.g. `02674b7ab946` → `02/674b7ab946/` |
69-| `git-refs` (default since CLI 0.10) | One ref per checkpoint: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` | The ref commit's tree root is the checkpoint | 26-char ULID (12-hex ids also occur) |
70-
71-- An empty `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch means the repo migrated to refs, so always try both backends.
72-- On refs, the ref commit's message carries the trailers `Checkpoint: <id>`, `Entire-Session: <uuid>`, `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit|import` and `Entire-Agent: <name>`.
73-- Commits on code branches link to a checkpoint with the trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`.
74-
75-### The tree of one checkpoint
76-
77-```
78-metadata.json                 checkpoint root: cli_version, checkpoint_id, strategy, branch, files_touched, sessions[], token_usage
79-<n>/metadata.json             one per session in this checkpoint (n = 0, 1, …)
80-<n>/full.jsonl                the agent's native transcript (best-effort redacted)
81-<n>/transcript.jsonl          Entire's compact transcript (CLI ≥ 0.10)
82-<n>/prompt.txt                user prompts joined by "\n\n---\n\n" (sometimes missing)
83-<n>/content_hash.txt          "sha256:<hex>" of full.jsonl
84-tasks/<tool_use_id>/          subagents: task.json, agent-<id>.jsonl
85-```
86-
87-- Paths in the root `sessions[]` are repo-absolute on the branch backend (`/02/674b7ab946/0/metadata.json`). Normalise them.
88-
89-### Session `metadata.json`: the keys we use
90-
91-| Key | Notes |
92-|---|---|
93-| `session_id` | The agent's own id. **The same session recurs across checkpoints.** Aggregate per session over all its checkpoints |
94-| `agent` | Display name: `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Copilot CLI`, `Factory AI Droid`, `Pi`, … |
95-| `model` | Often `""`. Fall back to the transcript (below) |
96-| `created_at` | RFC3339; roughly the commit time |
97-| `token_usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, api_call_count}` | Covers **this checkpoint's slice** of the transcript, not the whole session. `input_tokens` excludes cached input |
98-| `files_touched[]` | Repo-relative paths |
99-| `initial_attribution.{agent_lines, agent_removed, human_added, human_modified, human_removed, total_committed, agent_percentage}` | Entire's own agent-vs-human line attribution for the commit |
100-| `prompt_attributions[]` | Per-prompt line attribution, when present |
101-| `session_metrics.turn_count`, `strategy`, `branch`, `cli_version` | `strategy: "import"` marks history imported from before capture. Exclude it from any event-period analysis |
102-
103-- **Not recorded:** cost, a rules-file hash, the harness version (except inside transcripts), and the parent commit.
104-
105-### Recovering the model and the rules file from transcripts
106-
107-- **Claude Code `full.jsonl`:**
108-  - `type:"assistant"` lines carry `.message.model` and `.message.usage{input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens}`.
109-  - `type:"attachment"` with `attachment.type:"model"` carries `identity.modelId`, e.g. `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`.
110-  - `attachment.type:"instructions"` (`files[].{path,type,content}`) and `"nested_memory"` carry the **full text of the CLAUDE.md files loaded**. That's the rules file. Hash the `type: Project` entries.
111-- **Codex `full.jsonl`:**
112-  - `turn_context.payload.model`

content.text:
T16 is finished: the ledger script works, `check` flags a tag/setup mismatch, and all tests pass. It's committed as `bf8a989` on `task/T16`.

**What it does** (`scripts/ledger.ts`)
- **`record <Txx> <setup> <branch>`** writes the task's first ledger line. If `ROSTER_TASKS` is set, it rebuilds the prompt the same way `run-setup.sh` does (tag, then guardrails, then the rest of the task block) and stores its `prompt_sha256` and the tag.
- **`merged <Txx> <mergeSha>`** stores the full merge sha. It fails if the task was never recorded or the sha isn't a commit.
- **`sync`** finds a task's commits: the merged side of its merge commit, or the branch minus `main` if it isn't merged yet. From those it collects:
  - the checkpoint ids from `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers;
  - the session ids, read from the checkpoints in both storage backends;
  - the number of user prompts, without double-counting when a session's prompts repeat across checkpoints;
  - the number of `human:` commits;
  - the prompt tag, taken from the session's own first prompt. It only uses the tag saved by `record` if no session has one.
- **`check`** looks at every merged task and reports a missing checkpoint, a missing tag, or a tag whose setup or task doesn't match the ledger. It exits 1 if it finds any problem, 0 if clean, and 2 on bad usage.

**The ledger file:** `reports/self/tasks.jsonl` is append-only. Each line is a full copy of one task's state, and the latest line for a task is the current one; `sync` adds nothing if nothing changed. Each line has the fields you listed plus four extra ones: `prompt_tag` (needed for `check`), `session_ids` (what `sync` fills in), `event` and `at`. The file doesn't exist yet. The script creates it on the first real `record`, so none was committed.

**Tests:** `tests/ledger.test.ts` builds a temp git repo with fake trailers and checkpoints in both backends, based on the real samples.
- `bun test tests/ledger.test.ts`: 8 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test` (whole suite): 51 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.

The tests cover:
- a task with a mismatched tag, which `check` flags;
- a merged task with no checkpoint, which is flagged;
- an unmerged task, which is ignored;
- the bad-usage exit code from the command line.

**`src/types.ts`:** no change.

**`run-setup.sh` hook:** it already has the `record` call: `(cd "$ROOT" && bun scripts/ledger.ts record "$TASK" "$SETUP" "$BRANCH") || true`. Because `ROSTER_TASKS` is set in that script's environment, the prompt hash will be filled in. The one new line I'd propose is for the merge step, run after `git merge --no-ff task/Txx`:
```
bun scripts/ledger.ts merged "$TASK" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" && bun scripts/ledger.ts sync && bun scripts/ledger.ts check
```

**Unfinished:** `sync` only reads local refs. To pick up checkpoint refs from the remote, run `git fetch origin 'refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'` first.
